newsitem.title: UK: EMI up as publisher sale fuels takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: EMI up as publisher sale fuels takeover talk.

text.p: Shares in British music group EMI rose on Tuesday on speculation that U.S. group MCA Inc was seeking to raise funds for a takeover bid by selling its U.S. publisher Putnam Berkley, traders said.
On Tuesday, British media group Pearson said it had acquired Putnam Berkley from MCA for $336 million.
"MCA is considered the most likely bidder for EMI and people are thinking they (MCA) could be trying to drum up cash for a bid and that lifted EMI's shares," one marketmaker said.
EMI shares were up 30-1/2p at 1,365p in volume of just over 625,877 stocks. The broader market was up over half a percent.
Dealers said the move had focused attention on EMI but said they were sceptical of an imminent takeover bid.
"It's a good market story but they'd need more cash than that for EMI," a second marketmaker said.
Pearson shares were up one penny at 751p.
